title: Review: jmap-client crate — review-rusty-loop pass
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — no correctness bugs found. Two API-shape issues (non_exhaustive on ClientError, extract_response consuming JmapResponse) that must be fixed before extension crates lock in. URL scheme checking gap is real but low severity given validate_session_urls protection.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the SSE scan_from arithmetic (3-byte overlap) was verified by reading comments but not independently tested for CRLF straddling; if the overlap calculation is wrong, a frame delimiter could be missed. Uncertainty driven by: the SSE parser has no test exercising the scan_from path with CRLF at a chunk boundary — JMAP-xx7.6 captures this gap. Would raise confidence if: a test exercised CRLF block termination through the full subscribe_events stream (needs mock HTTP server returning chunked SSE with CRLF).
Idiom rating: CLEAN — no ownership misuse, no unsafe, no Box<dyn Error> in API, no .unwrap() in production code, no .len() == 0 antipatterns, no bare return as last expression. One clippy-level inconsistency (inline paths in request.rs, JMAP-xx7.13). Core design is idiomatic Rust.
Rust idiom confidence: 90% chance of no missed issue. Least confident flags: none — the code is clean. Uncertainty driven by: not running cargo clippy directly on the codebase; some clippy lints may catch patterns not visible by reading.
